findings.evidence: “When a run, a review or an execution step calls an external AI CLI and acts on the result.” This repeats the frontmatter without adding a decision or an exception.
findings.fix: Keep the activation guidance in the frontmatter and record the removal of the duplicate body section.

findings.evidence: “An execution lane's answer is the change to verify.” The chain step does not say how to verify an `ok` result when `coverage_unchecked` is present; even `coverage=1/1` can omit planned tasks.
findings.fix: Add an execute checkpoint before chaining: inspect the findings, reconcile unchecked tasks and uncommitted work against the original plan, and mark the plan complete only when that evidence supports it.

findings.evidence: “Use when you run, wait for, read, retry or chain an external AI CLI” covers dispatch and result handling but omits controlling herdr hosting, an explicit workflow and should-trigger case.
findings.fix: Use when launching, previewing, waiting for, diagnosing, retrying or resuming an external AI lane through ai-kit's cross-ai.mjs runner (pi, opencode, codex, cursor, copilot or claude). Use it to pass role, effort, context, session, skills or MCP settings; use --argv-file for an unsupported CLI; or choose herdr hosting or headless execution. Also use when a lane prints AIKIT-XAI, exits 69 or 75, hits quota or HTTP 429, reports ignored settings, locked or partial, includes retry_after_s=, or leaves GSD asking retry/skip/abort. Keep the owner-selected runtime, provider and model; follow the runner's wait and stop rules. Not for setting up reviewer rosters, configuring GSD or resuming the current chat.

findings.evidence: “The hard tier's schedule (`[runner.retry]`)” loads the schedule, reset arithmetic and six-key defaults table for every activation, although the caller acts on the emitted retry hint and the quota reference already carries the tuning details. The 399-line body contains over 6,000 words.
findings.fix: Keep the retry/no-retry decision, the one-shot scheduler guard and the owner handoff inline. Consolidate the schedule, key bounds, reset calculations and tuning examples in `references/subprocess-quota-policy.md`, with an explicit read trigger for configuring or explaining the retry ladder. Keep all attribution intact.

findings.evidence: “`$ROLE` is `review` for a review lane and `execute` only for a change the owner authorized.” The execute branch checks authorization for the change but not the lane's effective permissions; the sibling curated-config skill documents that the default execute formulas can run with full permissions.
findings.fix: Before an execute launch with a required write, shell or MCP boundary, preview the exact invocation with `--print-argv`. If effective access exceeds the approved scope or cannot be verified, require verified containment or stop; authorization for the edit is not authorization for unrestricted access.

findings.evidence: “Run plan-review.md as a review on opencode with the model fake/ok” has an empty `files` array and no fake runtime setup. The same-session and partial-resume assertions also omit the required preview and `session applied` gate.
findings.fix: Provide the launch prompt and a hermetic fake-runtime fixture, or make the case a preview-only exercise. Assert that resume previews the exact call and stops without spawning when the session setting is ignored.

findings.evidence: “Second opinion please: send docs/plans/parser-plan.md to codex as a review lane through cross-ai.mjs” still names the exact tool. The 10/10 set has useful negatives but few positives that test recognition without the runner's vocabulary.
findings.fix: Replace two direct positives with realistic requests that omit the runner and status tokens, such as asking for a second opinion from the project's configured external reviewer and for a follow-up in that reviewer's existing conversation.

findings.evidence: “Adds a path an execute result may not change” overstates `--forbid`. The linked `references/execute-checks.md` at line 14 says a changed path does not trigger `forbidden_path` if the prompt's `<files>` names it; the runner enforces that exemption.
findings.fix: Describe `--forbid` as a post-run check against changes to forbidden paths not authorized by the prompt's `<files>`, not a write barrier. Tell callers who need an absolute prohibition to require verified containment.

findings.evidence: “An exit 75 whose `AIKIT-XAI` line carries `retry_after_s=` is the hard tier,” followed by an unconditional wait. The sibling `references/lane-failure.md` at line 19 says the configured usage-limited review fallback runs before hard-tier handling; a successful switch schedules nothing. The exception at line 358 does not state that precedence.
findings.fix: Before choosing a wait or owner stop, branch on the flagged ai-kit-spec-review lane exception: if its configured quota fallback switches successfully, schedule nothing for the original lane; otherwise apply the regular exit routing.

findings.evidence: “A quota stop on a lane whose matched row carries a pool … or whose call passes `--pool` … writes one blocked-until record.” The linked quota policy at line 191 and `blockedAfterStop` both exclude confirmed router lanes, even with an explicit pool.
findings.fix: Limit the promise to non-router quota stops with a resolved pool. Instruct the caller to verify the actual `cross-ai: blocked-until` line or use `--blocked-status` before reporting that the pool was blocked.

findings.evidence: “Both are already on disk” assumes the shell wrote `lane.rc` and the runner finished its trailer. A hard kill or host timeout can leave either missing, and the exit table has no branch for missing or conflicting evidence.
findings.fix: After the launch ends, require an exit record and a matching terminal `AIKIT-XAI` line before applying the exit table. If either is missing or they disagree, report the host outcome and the available evidence as incomplete; do not merge, resume or schedule a retry from it.
